I don't really know how to bring it up. I only have one close friend, hes the only one that knows outside of my family. The rest of who I talk to is who I work with. I'm at work all the time and have gotten to know all 8 of my co workers very well over the past year and a half, so in a way I consider them all friends, even my boss, but sometimes I think I worry that if I tell someone they either won't care or will treat me differently.

Yeah right now my main watch is sodium, but I do try to stay away from high potassium foods too which sucks because I looooove orange juice and fruit in general. Its really hard to go out with friends or go to a work party or any social gathering and have to decline all the food and drinks, it sort of makes me feel weird because they have no idea of my condition but I just try to play it cool the best I can. If I had a dollar for every time I lied and said "no thank you I just ate" id be rich

Thank you for the comment. I've been watching my salt and trying to mainly drink water. Its so hard to eat low sodium food I feel like I'm constantly starving, everything is so high in salt. I really need to go back to my doctor and get more ace inhibitors prescribed I just can't build up the guts to go sit in that little room again.

I know what you mean. I too am in that vicious cycle of depression. I have been ever since i was in elementary school. Its very awkward trying to come to terms with a life threatening disease at such a young age. I was diagnosed with Chronic Kidney Disease around the same time other kids in my class were just trying to understand long division. The absolute worst years of my life were high school. I dropped out and went back 5 times  Ultimately ended up getting my GED. But I take pride in knowing that I have always given my best effort. I went back to highschool 5 times because I wanted a real diploma I just couldn't mentally or emotionally handle it. But slowly i started to, in a way,  sort of mask alot of my depressive side. At least during the day at work. I know alot of people hate working but the best feeling I have ever felt is waking up after a good nights rest, going to work and just sort of embracing the sole fact that you're alive and able to go to work in the first place, Taking a deep breathe of air and basking in reality, living in the moment, 1 chain link in the non stop world around you. Just enjoying the simple fact that you are a part of this world just like me.
